title: Residue fields of closed points
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme of
finite type over a field
$K$, and let $x\in X$.

1. **(a)** $x$ is a closed point of
$X$ if and only if
$\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)=0$, i.e. if and only if
$\kappa(x)$ is finite over $K$ (Zariski's lemma: a field
finitely generated, as an algebra, over $K$ is finite over $K$).
1. **(b)** If $K$ is separably closed and $x$ is closed, then
$\kappa(x)/K$ is finite and purely inseparable and $\kappa(x)$ is
separably closed.

proof.text: (1) Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be any affine open subset of $X$ containing $x$; finite type over $K$ makes $A$ a finitely generated $K$-algebra, $x$ corresponds to a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, $\kappa(x)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$, and $x$ is closed in $U$ exactly when $\mathfrak p$ is maximal. Step (2) shows, for every such $U$, that $x$ is closed in $U$ if and only if $\kappa(x)$ is finite over $K$; the latter condition does not depend on $U$. Since a subset of $X$ is closed if and only if its intersection with each member of an affine open cover is closed, and $\{x\}\cap V=\emptyset$ for an open $V\not\ni x$, the point $x$ is closed in $X$ if and only if it is closed in every affine open containing it, i.e. if and only if $\kappa(x)$ is finite over $K$. (2) If $\mathfrak p$ is maximal, $A/\mathfrak p$ is a field generated by the images of finitely many $K$-algebra generators of $A$, so [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] gives that $\kappa(x)=A/\mathfrak p$ is finite over $K$. Conversely, if $\kappa(x)$ is finite over $K$, then the domain $A/\mathfrak p$ is a $K$-subspace of the finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $\kappa(x)$, hence itself finite-dimensional. For every nonzero $a\in A/\mathfrak p$, multiplication by $a$ is an injective $K$-linear endomorphism of $A/\mathfrak p$ (a domain) and hence is surjective, so $ab=1$ for some $b\in A/\mathfrak p$; thus $A/\mathfrak p$ is a field and $\mathfrak p$ is maximal. (3) For a finitely generated field extension, [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis] supplies a finite transcendence basis. The extension is finite exactly when this basis is empty: finiteness forces every element to be algebraic, while if the basis is empty, the finitely many field generators are algebraic and adjoining them one at a time gives a finite extension. Thus finite over $K$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)=0$. (4) If $K$ is separably closed and $x$ is closed, part (a) gives a finite extension $\kappa(x)/K$. Then [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-purely-inseparable] gives that this extension is purely inseparable, and [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-sep-closed] gives that $\kappa(x)$ is separably closed.
